source.title: Nmap and Wireshark Lab: -sS capture
source.reuse_conditions: No repository license was found. The PCAP is not redistributed; only measurements and port numbers are retained.

capture.topology: Single local IPv4 scanner and target; README reports Netcat listeners on TCP 80, 143, and 995; other network details unknown
capture.tool_profile: Nmap -sS -F, per source README; exact full command and Nmap version unknown
capture.sensor: Wireshark capture; version, capture interface, and snap length unknown
capture.extraction: tools/inspect_pcapng.py: Ethernet/IPv4/TCP only; scanner-to-target TCP SYN without ACK; responses matched by target source port; no external labels trusted

comparison_tolerances.packet_and_byte_totals: exactly 203 packets: 3 open ports with 120 outbound + 58 inbound bytes, 97 closed ports with 60 outbound + 54 inbound bytes
comparison_tolerances.probe_span_ms: 9 to 14; millisecond event timestamps round the measured 11.2165 ms window
comparison_tolerances.response_delay_ms: generated values within measured 0.002 to 0.243 ms; distribution is approximate
comparison_tolerances.application_exchanges: zero; SYN scan does not establish an application session

implementation_assumptions: The captured port set and outcome distribution are transplanted onto one synthetic inventory host with a service override for ports 80, 143, and 995
Probe order is shuffled per seed; exact wire order is not retained
The capture is a small single-target lab trace and does not calibrate the other scenario families, typical enterprise scanning, or source-compatible sensor schemas
